title: Distinct Gate Paths to LCA
summary: Inputs n,parent,gates,queries. gates[u]=[redCount,blueCount,whiteCount]; query=[aNode,aCard,bNode,bCard], with red=1 and blue=0. Each upward move chooses exactly one gate instance at its departing node. Red accepts red and preserves it; blue accepts blue and preserves it; white accepts either and flips it. Equal-colored parallel gates count separately. There are no extra stationary gate uses. Stop at the LCA without using its gates. Each person already there has one empty path. Multiply independent path counts modulo 1000000007 for each query; XOR those residues.

clarification: The loose phrase about using white gates repeatedly means across moves, not infinitely many color flips before one move. Authored illustration: a red-card traveler one edge below the LCA with gates [2,0,3] has five ways, including three ending blue; matching final colors is not required.
constraintsReportedBySource: 2<=n<=20000; parent and gates length n; parent[0]=-1; other parents valid node IDs forming a tree; gate counts 0..10; 1..20000 queries.
